title: Piku's missing postcard
subtitle: A tiny Charminar adventure, without leaving home.
fact: Charminar is a Hyderabad landmark with four minarets (towers).
fiction: Piku and the missing postcard are make-believe. The landmark is real.

steps.label: Meet Piku
steps.title: A very small emergency
steps.read: Piku the pigeon landed on the windowsill with a crumpled envelope. ‘I promised to send my cousin a postcard of Hyderabad. But the wind has carried my picture away! {name}, will you help me make a new one?’
steps.hinglish: Piku ko Hyderabad ka postcard banana hai. {name}, kya tum uski madad karoge?
steps.do: Read the invitation, then let your child choose Piku's voice. A pigeon can sound however you like.
steps.little: Ask: ‘Shall we help Piku?’ A nod, a point, or a funny pigeon face all count.
steps.big: Ask: ‘If you sent someone a picture of our city, what would you want them to remember?’
steps.quiet: Use a whisper for Piku. Your child can answer with a thumbs-up.
steps.wiggles: Make two little wing movements while staying on the floor. No flapping race required.
steps.parent: There is no correct performance. If the story isn't landing, skip straight to drawing together.

steps.label: Find four
steps.title: The clue with four corners
steps.read: ‘I remember FOUR towers,’ said Piku. ‘One, two, three... oh, I keep forgetting the last one!’ Piku needs a very good four-finder.
steps.hinglish: Charminar ke chaar towers hain. Chalo, ek saath chaar ginte hain.
steps.do: Find the four corners of your sheet. Touch each corner once while counting together. Keep the sheet whole.
steps.little: You point, your child follows. Count slowly to four; starting again is part of the game.
steps.big: Ask your child to show four another way: four fingers, four dots, or two pairs of marks.
steps.quiet: Tap the four corners softly with a fingertip. No sounds needed.
steps.wiggles: Draw four big imaginary corners in the air with your hands, then return to your paper.
steps.parent: One real city fact: Charminar has four minarets. Your paper is a pretend model, not an architectural plan.

steps.label: Borrow a colour
steps.title: A postcard needs a little life
steps.read: Piku tilted his head. ‘My picture is still looking rather... paper-coloured. Could we borrow a colour from your room? Only borrow it with our eyes. Nothing needs to leave its home!’
steps.hinglish: Apne aas-paas ek rang dhoondo. Bas dekho aur uska rang yaad rakho.
steps.do: Choose a colour you can see nearby. Put that colour somewhere on the postcard, or tell the grown-up where it belongs.
steps.little: Offer two colours you can already see. Let your child point, choose, or scribble.
steps.big: Choose two colours and invent a city detail for each: a shop sign, a kite, a doorway, or anything imagined.
steps.quiet: Play an ‘I spy’ game with pointing instead of calling out.
steps.wiggles: Take four slow steps together to look for a colour, staying in the same clear room. Looking from your seat works too.
steps.parent: No collecting objects, opening cupboards, or climbing. Every part of the mission can be done sitting down.

steps.label: Make the postcard
steps.title: Your Hyderabad, on paper
steps.read: ‘Four towers, a borrowed colour, and something only you could imagine,’ cooed Piku. ‘That is exactly the kind of postcard I was hoping for.’
steps.hinglish: Ab apna Hyderabad banao. Chaar towers, ek rang, aur tumhari apni kahani.
steps.do: Make four tall marks for towers, add your colour, then draw one wonderfully made-up thing. A giant mango? A flying bus? This is your story-city.
steps.little: A grown-up can make four tall marks first. Your child adds any marks they like. No tracing or neatness needed.
steps.big: Add a doorway and invent what Piku might see through it. Tell a one-sentence story about your picture.
steps.quiet: Draw together side by side. Piku is happy to watch in silence.
steps.wiggles: Before drawing, make yourself as tall as a tower, then as small as a pigeon. Standing is optional.
steps.parent: This is art and pretend play, not a test of drawing Charminar correctly. Describe what you notice instead of correcting the picture.

steps.label: Send Piku home
steps.title: A very important delivery
steps.read: Piku admired the new postcard. ‘This has something my old one didn't: YOUR imagination.’ He tucked the picture under a pretend wing. ‘Next time you see a tower, think of me. And remember to count all four!’
steps.hinglish: Piku ka postcard taiyaar hai! Isme tumhari imagination bhi hai.
steps.do: Give your postcard a name. Pretend to deliver it to a family member, or keep it somewhere your child chooses. The real picture stays with you.
steps.little: Ask: ‘Which part do you want to show me?’ Let your child point or explain in any way.
steps.big: Ask: ‘What was real about our city, and what did we make up?’ Both belong in a story, but they are different.
steps.quiet: Send Piku off with a silent wave. You can celebrate without a cheer.
steps.wiggles: Walk the postcard to its new home together, then give Piku one last imaginary wing-wave.
steps.parent: A short adventure counts. If your child stopped earlier, the unfinished postcard can wait for another day.
